Reproducing Sargolini et al. (2006) from dandiset 000582¶

Paper: Sargolini F, Fyhn M, Hafting T, McNaughton BL, Witter MP, Moser M-B, Moser EI (2006). Conjunctive representation of position, direction, and velocity in entorhinal cortex. Science 312:758-762. doi:10.1126/science.1125572

Data: DANDI:000582, version 0.251111.2151, streamed from the archive. Nothing is downloaded to disk.

Why this version. The paper cites no version of the dandiset. 0.251111.2151 is the only published version, and the draft (last modified 2026-05-28) holds the same 118 assets, with the same sizes and asset identifiers, so there is no newer content to test. The earlier attempt, 000582-sargolini-2006-01, used the same version.

Claims. The claims file is claims/000582/10.1126-science.1125572.yaml, written by a reader from the version of record and its Supporting Online Material (SOM), and checked by a second reader. It replaces a file written from the abstract only. The three claims of the earlier attempt keep their ids (layer2-grid, deep-hd-conjunctive, speed) and now carry the paper's numbers and criteria. This notebook tests the claims file as it stands; where it leaves a detail open, every reading it names is run. This attempt asked five questions about the claims file (questions/000582.yaml); a reader answered them on 2026-10-20, the claims file now carries the answers, and this notebook follows the updated criteria. This version also answers the verifier's first-round report (transcripts/000582/verifier-1-report.md): it adds the outputs the report asked for, and one outcome changed (grid-phase-orientation, see its section). It then answers the second-round report (transcripts/000582/verifier-2-report.md), which agreed with every outcome: it corrects the conclusions the report quoted, and adds the outputs it asked for. No outcome changes.

The measures follow the SOM as the claims file quotes it, and are defined in sargolini.py next to this notebook, with the source of each parameter.

Readings. The claims file names readings for details the paper leaves open (O1 to O4): trials pooled or the first trial (O1), 3 cm maps with peaks of 25 bins or 1.5 cm maps with peaks of 100 pixels (O2), the gridness circle to the outermost peak's edge or its centre, and the central peak removed as its pixels or as a disc (O3), with a peak's centre its pixel of highest correlation or its centroid and its radius that of a disc of the same area or the largest distance from its centre to one of its pixels (O3, as answered), and a significance level of 0.05 or 0.01 for the head-direction tests (O4). The peak radius is not used when the circle runs to the outer peak's centre and the central peak is removed as its pixels, so that pair of readings is run once. That gives 56 combinations for grid cells, 4 for head-direction cells and 112 for conjunctive cells; every claim is shown under all of them.

LAYERS = ["II", "III", "V", "VI"]
DEEP = ["III", "V", "VI"]


def within(value, expected, tolerance):
    return bool(abs(value - expected) <= tolerance + 1e-12)


def outcome_of(outcomes):
    """The outcome all readings give, or methods_underspecified when they differ."""
    found = sorted(set(outcomes))
    return found[0] if len(found) == 1 else "methods_underspecified (" + ", ".join(found) + ")"

Data check¶

Each file is one recording: the positions of one or two tracking LEDs and the spike times of the cells recorded. The units table gives each cell's name (tetrode and cell), layer, electrode depth and hemisphere. The electrodes table has one row per file, with location "MEC" and no coordinates. There is no trial table and no other annotation.

In [2]:
sessions = sg.load_sessions()
units = pd.DataFrame([
    dict(subject=s.subject, path=s.path, session=s.session_id, unit=u.name, layer=u.layer or "not given",
         depth_mm=u.depth_mm, hemisphere=u.hemisphere or "not given", two_leds=s.green is not None,
         minutes=int(round(s.duration / 60)), spikes=len(u.spike_times),
         rate_hz=len(u.spike_times) / s.duration)
    for s in sessions for u in s.units])
print(f"{len(sessions)} files, {units.subject.nunique()} rats, {len(units)} cell-sessions\n")
print("Files and cells by number of LEDs and file length:")

                                                 rats=("subject", "nunique")).to_string())

      f"file lengths {min(s.duration for s in sessions):.1f} to {max(s.duration for s in sessions):.1f} s")

The enclosure and the scale of the positions¶

Every file says the rat ran in a 1 x 1 m enclosure. The SOM lists four enclosures: circles of 90 and 180 cm and squares of 100 and 150 cm. Below, for each file: the span of the tracked positions, whether they are centred so that the minimum is exactly minus half the larger span (which would mean they were rescaled), the distance between the two LEDs (7 cm in the SOM, a check of the scale that does not depend on the enclosure), and the fraction of samples in the corners outside the inscribed circle (near zero in a circular enclosure). For the two-LED files, the fraction of samples with the LEDs more than 15 cm apart, over twice the SOM's 7 cm, flags files where head direction from the two LEDs is doubtful (15 cm is a display threshold, not a selection).

In [3]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    span = np.nanmax(s.red, axis=0) - np.nanmin(s.red, axis=0)
    big = span.max()
    centred = np.isclose(np.nanmin(s.red[:, np.argmax(span)]), -big / 2, atol=0.01)
    centre = (np.nanmax(s.red, axis=0) + np.nanmin(s.red, axis=0)) / 2
    r = np.hypot(*(s.red - centre).T)
    sep = np.hypot(*(s.green - s.red).T) if s.green is not None else np.array([np.nan])
    sep_ok = sep[~np.isnan(sep)]
    rows.append(dict(path=s.path, subject=s.subject, minutes=int(round(s.duration / 60)),
                     span_x=span[0], span_y=span[1], larger_span=round(big, 1), centred=centred,
                     led_separation=np.nanmedian(sep),
                     led_over_15cm=np.mean(sep_ok > 15) if s.green is not None else np.nan,
                     outside_circle=np.nanmean(r > big / 2 + 1)))
extent = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Files by larger span of positions (cm) and file length:")
print(extent.groupby(["larger_span", "minutes"]).agg(
    files=("path", "size"), rats=("subject", "nunique"), all_centred=("centred", "all"),
    median_led_separation_cm=("led_separation", "median"),
    median_outside_circle=("outside_circle", "median"), max_outside_circle=("outside_circle", "max")).round(3).to_string())
sep = extent.led_separation.dropna()
print(f"\nLED separation, median per file: {sep.min():.1f} to {sep.max():.1f} cm (median {sep.median():.1f}); SOM: 7 cm")
print(f"Files whose positions span exactly 100, 150 or 200 cm on the larger axis: "
      f"{extent.larger_span.isin([100.0, 150.0, 200.0]).sum()} of {len(extent)}")
print("Files with fewer than 1% of samples outside the inscribed circle (a circular enclosure), by span:",
      extent[extent.outside_circle < 0.01].groupby("larger_span").size().to_dict(), "of",
      extent.groupby("larger_span").size().to_dict())
print("Two-LED files with the LEDs more than 15 cm apart (over twice the SOM's 7 cm) in over 10% of samples:")
print(extent[extent.led_over_15cm > 0.1][["path", "larger_span", "led_separation", "led_over_15cm"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"Other two-LED files: at most {extent.led_over_15cm[extent.led_over_15cm <= 0.1].max():.3f} of samples above 15 cm")
others = extent[extent.led_over_15cm <= 0.5].led_separation
print(f"The other {len(others)} two-LED files (LEDs over 15 cm apart in at most half of the samples): median separation "
      f"{others.min():.1f} to {others.max():.1f} cm")

Trials¶

The SOM says every rat ran two 10-minute trials, 10 minutes apart. 95 files last 10 minutes and 23 last 20 minutes. Below, the step between successive position samples at 600 s in the 20-minute files, against the 99th percentile of all steps in the same file: a jump at 600 s marks two trials joined end to end.

In [4]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if len(s.trials) == 2:
        ok = ~np.isnan(s.red).any(axis=1)
        before = s.red[ok & (s.t < sg.TRIAL_S - 0.1)][-1]
        after = s.red[ok & (s.t >= sg.TRIAL_S + 0.1)][0]
        steps = np.hypot(*(s.red[10:] - s.red[:-10]).T)          # displacements over 0.2 s
        first = (s.t >= s.trials[0][0]) & (s.t < sg.TRIAL_S)
        centre_1 = (np.nanmax(s.red[first], axis=0) + np.nanmin(s.red[first], axis=0)) / 2
        centre_2 = (np.nanmax(s.red[~first], axis=0) + np.nanmin(s.red[~first], axis=0)) / 2
        rows.append(dict(file=s.path.split("/")[1][:22], step_599_9_to_600_1_cm=np.hypot(*(after - before)),
                         p99_9_of_0_2s_steps_cm=np.nanpercentile(steps, 99.9),
                         trial1_centre_offset_cm=np.hypot(*centre_1), trial2_centre_offset_cm=np.hypot(*centre_2)))
joins = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(joins.round(2).to_string())
print(f"\n{(joins.step_599_9_to_600_1_cm > joins.p99_9_of_0_2s_steps_cm).sum()} of {len(joins)} files move farther "
      f"from 599.9 to 600.1 s than in 99.9% of their 0.2-s steps; the first trial's positions are centred "
      f"on zero (within 0.1 cm) in {(joins.trial1_centre_offset_cm < 0.1).sum()}, the second's in "
      f"{(joins.trial2_centre_offset_cm < 0.1).sum()}.")
same_day = units.assign(day=units.session.str[:6]).groupby(["subject", "day"]).path.nunique()
print(f"Days with more than one file: {(same_day > 1).sum()}; the files of a day are listed below.")

Recordings deposited more than once, and the identity of cells across files¶

Identical spike trains or identical position tracks in two files would be a recording deposited twice. Cells are listed per file; no identifier links a cell across files. Cells of the same rat with the same electrode depth, hemisphere and tetrode-cell name in several files may be the same cell recorded on several days.

In [5]:
spike_hash = Counter(hashlib.md5(np.round(u.spike_times, 6).tobytes()).hexdigest()
                     for s in sessions for u in s.units)
track_hash = Counter(hashlib.md5(np.nan_to_num(s.red).tobytes()).hexdigest() for s in sessions)
print(f"Spike trains deposited more than once: {sum(v > 1 for v in spike_hash.values())}; "
      f"position tracks deposited more than once: {sum(v > 1 for v in track_hash.values())}")

Measures for every cell¶

The next cell computes, for every cell, the rate maps, autocorrelograms and gridness, the head-direction tuning and its tests, and the speed regressions, under every reading, and for every pair of cells recorded together the offset of their rate-map crosscorrelogram (sargolini.py).

In [7]:
with ProcessPoolExecutor(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1)) as pool:
    results = list(pool.map(sg.session_measures, sessions, chunksize=1))
cells = pd.DataFrame([c for cs, _ in results for c in cs])
pairs = pd.DataFrame([p for _, ps in results for p in ps])
by_path = {s.path: s for s in sessions}
print(f"{len(cells)} cells and {len(pairs)} pairs of simultaneously recorded cells")
no_score = {g: int(cells[f"grid|{t}|{g}"].isna().sum()) for t in sg.TRIALS for g in sg.GRID_READINGS}
print(f"Cells without a gridness (no autocorrelogram peak besides the central one): "
      f"{min(no_score.values())} to {max(no_score.values())} of {len(cells)}, by reading")
two_led = cells[cells.two_leds]
print(f"Two-LED cells without a Watson U2 or block correlation: "
      f"{int(two_led['u2|pooled'].isna().sum())} and {int(two_led['block_r|pooled'].isna().sum())} of {len(two_led)}")

Do spikes and positions share a clock?¶

There are no trials or events to align to, so the check shifts each cell's spike train against the tracking by -2 to +2 s and recomputes the measures the claims rest on: Watson's U2 for the 30 two-LED cells with the highest U2, and the spatial information of the 3 cm rate map for the 30 cells with the highest gridness. If the clocks agree, both peak at a shift near zero; an offset between them would move the peak.

In [8]:
lags = np.round(np.arange(-2, 2.01, 0.25), 2)
top_hd = cells[cells.two_leds].nlargest(30, "u2|pooled")
top_grid = cells.nlargest(30, f"grid|pooled|{sg.GRID_READINGS[0]}")
unit_of = {(s.path, u.name): (s, u) for s in sessions for u in s.units}
u2_lag = np.array([sg.lagged_u2(*unit_of[(r.path, r.unit)], lags) for r in top_hd.itertuples()])
info_lag = np.array([sg.lagged_map_info(*unit_of[(r.path, r.unit)], lags) for r in top_grid.itertuples()])
clock = pd.DataFrame({"shift_s": lags,
                      "median U2 / U2 at 0": np.median(u2_lag / u2_lag[:, [list(lags).index(0)]], axis=0),
                      "median info / info at 0": np.median(info_lag / info_lag[:, [list(lags).index(0)]], axis=0)})
print(clock.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nShift of the peak, per cell: U2 {Counter(lags[np.argmax(u2_lag, axis=1)]).most_common()}; "
      f"spatial information {Counter(lags[np.argmax(info_lag, axis=1)]).most_common()}")
print(f"Cells: {top_hd.subject.nunique()} rats and {top_hd.path.nunique()} files (U2); "
      f"{top_grid.subject.nunique()} rats and {top_grid.path.nunique()} files (information)")

The findings of attempt 000582-sargolini-2006-01, and new ones¶

The version is the same as the earlier attempt's, and the data are unchanged, so each finding is re-checked on the same files with the outputs above.

Finding of -01 Kind Status Shown by
Every file says the enclosure was 1 x 1 m, but in 23 sessions the positions span 1.5 to 2.5 m metadata_error Still present Enclosure table: 2 files span 150 cm and 20 span 200 cm on the larger axis, 19 of the 20 circular (under 1% of samples outside the inscribed circle)
The descriptions say position is given for two LEDs, but 47 of 118 files have one metadata_error Still present First table: 47 files, 167 cell-sessions with one LED; rat 11084 has files of both kinds
No identifier links a cell across files identifier_missing Still present 584 cell-sessions with a depth form 425 distinct (rat, depth, hemisphere, name), 99 of them in 2 to 7 files
The dandiset is a sample whose selection is not described selection_undocumented Still present 620 cell-sessions against the paper's 627 cells, 15 rats against 17, layer II 71 against 108 while layers III, V and VI hold slightly more than table S1A
The paper is not open access and the dandiset gives no analysis parameters methods_unavailable Partly fixed This attempt read the methods in the SOM, supplied by a person; the paper is still not open access, the dandiset states no parameter, and no analysis code is public

New findings:

  • The positions are rescaled. In all 118 files the positions span exactly 100, 150 or 200 cm on the larger axis, and the first trial is centred on zero. Of the 20 files spanning 200 cm, 19 look circular; the SOM's large circle is 180 cm across, so in those files distances and speeds are about 11% too large. The distance between the two LEDs (median 5.2 cm per file, 2.6 to 36 cm, against 7 cm in the SOM) is too variable to fix the scale. The files do not say that the positions were rescaled.
  • The 23 twenty-minute files hold two 10-minute trials joined near 600 s: in all 23 the position jumps between 599.9 and 600.1 s by more than 99.9% of the file's 0.2-s steps, and only the first trial is centred. There is no trial table, and nothing says which 10-minute files, if any, are the two trials of one recording; the files of a day differ in depth or cells (list above).
  • No file gives the recording sites' distance from the postrhinal border, which the paper's dorsoventral analyses use; depth is the depth the electrodes were lowered to.
  • No file names its enclosure, a condition or the cue-card position, so the cue-rotation trials cannot be found.
  • Six cells have no layer, 36 no depth and 230 no hemisphere.
  • The descriptions disagree with the files: the experiment description says the sample holds "conjunctive cells and head direction cells from layers III and V", the dandiset description that it holds spike times "for recorded grid cells"; the files hold cells of layers II, III, V and VI and of every class.
  • The electrodes table holds one row per file, location "MEC", with no coordinates, so it does not give the recording sites' distance from the postrhinal border either.
  • In two two-LED files, sub-11265_ses-09020601 and sub-11278_ses-31080502, the LEDs are more than 15 cm apart in 71% and 62% of samples (median 36.0 and 22.7 cm, against 2.6 to 8.4 cm in the other two-LED files), so head direction there is doubtful; nothing in the files flags it. They hold 13 layer III and 11 layer II cells. A third file, sub-11025_ses-06050501, has 17.8% of samples above 15 cm; the others at most 3.9%.
  • The files do not say which LED is the red one, whose positions the SOM uses. LED1 is the only LED in the single-LED files, and the SOM says single-LED rats carried a red LED, so LED1 is taken as red.

Spikes and positions are consistent with a shared clock: Watson's U2 and the spatial information peak at zero shift for 29 and 28 of 30 cells, and the 10 spikes outside the tracked period fall after the last sample.

Claim layer2-grid¶

The proportion of cells with grid structure depended on layer. Most well-separated layer II cells were grid cells (66 of 108), against a smaller proportion in layers III (78 of 223), V (17 of 110) and VI (42 of 186).

Criterion: all cells of all rats, by layer; a grid cell has gridness above 0, under readings O1 to O3. Reproduced when the layer II fraction is above 0.5 and above that of each deeper layer, and the four fractions are within tolerance (0.611 +/- 0.061, 0.350 +/- 0.035, 0.155 +/- 0.015, 0.226 +/- 0.023); partially reproduced when the order holds but a fraction is outside tolerance. Each cell-session counts as a cell, as the paper's 627 cells are about as many as the dandiset's 620 cell-sessions (data check). The six cells with no layer are left out. Two variants, which do not decide the outcome, follow the main table: the gridness of each cell's spike train shifted in time, a control for how often gridness above 0 arises without a grid, and the fractions with each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) counted once.

EXPECTED_GRID = {"II": (0.611, 0.061), "III": (0.350, 0.035), "V": (0.155, 0.015), "VI": (0.226, 0.023)}
known = cells[cells.layer.isin(LAYERS)].copy()
n_layer = known.layer.value_counts()
rows = []
for T, G, _ in sg.readings(with_level=False):
    grid = sg.classify(known, T, G, 0.05).grid
    frac = grid.groupby(known.layer).mean()
    order = frac["II"] > 0.5 and all(frac["II"] > frac[l] for l in DEEP)
    tol = all(within(frac[l], *EXPECTED_GRID[l]) for l in LAYERS)
    rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, **{l: frac[l] for l in LAYERS},
                     **{f"n {l}": int(grid[known.layer == l].sum()) for l in LAYERS}, total=int(grid.sum()),
                     order=order, in_tolerance=[l for l in LAYERS if within(frac[l], *EXPECTED_GRID[l])],
                     outcome="reproduced" if order and tol else "partially_reproduced" if order else "not_reproduced"))
grid_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Cells per layer:", n_layer[LAYERS].to_dict())
print(grid_table.round(3).to_string())
print(f"\nRange over the {len(grid_table)} readings:", {l: f"{grid_table[l].min():.3f} to {grid_table[l].max():.3f}" for l in LAYERS})
print("Expected:", {l: f"{v - t:.3f} to {v + t:.3f}" for l, (v, t) in EXPECTED_GRID.items()})
print("Readings with each layer within tolerance:", {l: int(grid_table.in_tolerance.apply(lambda x: l in x).sum()) for l in LAYERS})
print("Outcomes:", grid_table.outcome.value_counts().to_dict(), "->", outcome_of(grid_table.outcome))

# Variants that do not decide the outcome. (1) A control for gridness above 0: the same gridness
# for each cell's spike train shifted in time (sargolini.shifted_gridness), first reading.
seeds = np.random.default_rng(5820).integers(2**32, size=len(sessions))      # this section's own generator
with ProcessPoolExecutor(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1)) as pool:
    shifted = pd.DataFrame([r for rs in pool.map(sg.shifted_gridness, sessions, seeds, chunksize=1) for r in rs])
shifted = shifted.merge(known[["path", "unit", "layer"]], on=["path", "unit"])
print(f"Spike trains shifted in time, 5 shifts of 20 s or more per cell: {len(shifted)} maps of {shifted[['path', 'unit']].drop_duplicates().shape[0]} cells, "
      f"{int(shifted.gridness.isna().sum())} without a gridness")
print(f"  gridness above 0: {(shifted.gridness > 0).mean():.3f} of shifted maps; by layer "
      f"{(shifted.gridness > 0).groupby(shifted.layer).mean().round(3).to_dict()}")
print(f"  observed, gridness above 0: {known.grid.groupby(known.layer).mean().round(3).to_dict()}")
for q in (0.95, 0.99):
    cut = shifted.gridness.quantile(q)
    above = (known[col] > cut).groupby(known.layer).mean()
    print(f"  cells above the {q:.0%} point of the shifted gridness ({cut:.3f}): {above.round(3).to_dict()}; "
          f"layer II above every deeper layer: {all(above['II'] > above[l] for l in DEEP)}")
# (2) Each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) counted once, first file kept, under every reading.
first_copy = known.depth_mm.notna() & ~known.duplicated(["subject", "depth_mm", "hemisphere", "unit"])
once = known[first_copy]
rows, per_rat_rows = [], []
for T, G, _ in sg.readings(with_level=False):
    grid = sg.classify(once, T, G, 0.05).grid
    frac = grid.groupby(once.layer).mean()
    rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, **{l: frac[l] for l in LAYERS},
                     order=frac["II"] > 0.5 and all(frac["II"] > frac[l] for l in DEEP),
                     layers_in_tolerance=sum(within(frac[l], *EXPECTED_GRID[l]) for l in LAYERS)))
    per_rat_rows.append(grid.groupby([once.subject, once.layer]).sum().rename("grid"))
once_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"\nEach (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once: {len(once)} of {len(known)} cells "
      f"({int(known.depth_mm.isna().sum())} without a depth left out), over the {len(once_table)} readings:")
print("  fractions:", {l: f"{once_table[l].min():.3f} to {once_table[l].max():.3f}" for l in LAYERS},
      f"order holds under {int(once_table.order.sum())}; readings by number of layers within tolerance:",
      once_table.layers_in_tolerance.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
per_rat_once = pd.concat(per_rat_rows, axis=1)
per_rat_once = pd.DataFrame({"cells": once.groupby(["subject", "layer"]).size(),
                             "grid cells, fewest": per_rat_once.min(axis=1), "grid cells, most": per_rat_once.max(axis=1)})
print("Per rat and layer, each cell once, grid cells over the readings:")
print(per_rat_once.unstack("layer").fillna("").to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. Under all 56 readings layer II has the largest fraction of grid cells, 0.592 to 0.718, above 0.5 and above layers III (0.529 to 0.604), V (0.297 to 0.415) and VI (0.354 to 0.485), so the order holds. The layer II fraction is within its tolerance under 32 of the 56 readings, but no deeper layer is within tolerance under any reading: each is well above the paper's fraction. Gridness above 0 makes 277 to 329 cells grid cells, against the paper's 203 of 627. Per rat, the layer II fractions are 0.41 to 0.90 and the deeper ones 0 to 0.67; of the two rats recorded in layers II and III, layer II is higher in 10884 (0.60 against 0.43) and lower in 11265 (0.62 against 0.67).

Gridness above 0 is a lax criterion on these data. With each spike train shifted in time, 0.297 of the shifted maps have gridness above 0 (0.288 to 0.307 by layer), against observed fractions of 0.634, 0.559, 0.314 and 0.359 in layers II, III, V and VI under the first reading. In layers V and VI the observed fractions are barely above those of the shifted spike trains. Counting only cells above the 95% point of the shifted gridness (0.216) gives 0.408, 0.419, 0.186 and 0.197, and above the 99% point (0.362) 0.296, 0.348, 0.153 and 0.192. Under either stricter cut layer III is above layer II, so the layer order on which the partial outcome rests does not survive a stricter grid threshold, and no layer has a majority of grid cells. This is not the paper's criterion, and the outcome rests on gridness above 0, as the claim says; but it limits what the partial outcome shows.

Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once (425 of 614 cells; the 30 without a depth left out), the order holds under all 56 readings (layer II 0.680 to 0.780, III 0.451 to 0.564, V 0.333 to 0.437, VI 0.316 to 0.458), and no reading has all four layers within tolerance, so this variant gives the same outcome.

The answer on a peak's centre and radius adds the radius as the largest distance to a pixel of the peak. The outcome is the same under every reading, as before; the ranges widen a little (layer II 0.620 to 0.718 before).

The earlier attempt also called this claim partially reproduced, for another reason: it used a grid score of its own with a shuffled-data threshold, under which a third of layer II cells were grid cells. With the paper's criterion, gridness above 0, most layer II cells are grid cells, and the claim falls short on the deeper layers' fractions.

Claim grid-all-layers¶

Grid cells with tessellating firing fields were found in all four principal cell layers of MEC (II, III, V and VI).

Criterion: grid cells as in layer2-grid; reproduced when at least one grid cell is found in each layer.

Claim gridness-range-similar¶

Among deeper-layer cells with periodic firing, the range of gridness did not differ from that of layer II cells.

Criterion: a claim of absence with no test named by the paper. Grid cells of each layer (readings O1 to O3). Readings of the test: (a) two-sided Mann-Whitney, layer II against layers III to VI pooled; (b) Kruskal-Wallis across the four layers; each at p < 0.05. Reproduced when no reading finds a difference, not reproduced when all do, methods_underspecified when they disagree.

def range_tests(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, G, _ in sg.readings(with_level=False):
        col = f"grid|{T}|{G}"
        g = frame[sg.classify(frame, T, G, 0.05).grid]
        by = {l: g[g.layer == l][col] for l in LAYERS}
        mw = stats.mannwhitneyu(by["II"], g[g.layer != "II"][col], alternative="two-sided").pvalue
        kw = stats.kruskal(*by.values()).pvalue
        pairwise = {f"pair {x}-{y} p": stats.mannwhitneyu(by[x], by[y], alternative="two-sided").pvalue
                    for x, y in combinations(LAYERS, 2)}
        rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, mann_whitney_p=mw, kruskal_wallis_p=kw,
                         **{f"median {l}": by[l].median() for l in LAYERS},
                         **{f"range {l}": f"{by[l].min():.2f} to {by[l].max():.2f}" for l in LAYERS}, **pairwise))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

range_table = range_tests(known)
print(range_table.drop(columns=[c for c in range_table if c.startswith("pair ")]).round(4).to_string())
tests = pd.concat([range_table.mann_whitney_p, range_table.kruskal_wallis_p])
print(f"\nTests finding a difference (p < 0.05): {int((tests < 0.05).sum())} of {len(tests)} "
      f"(Mann-Whitney {int((range_table.mann_whitney_p < 0.05).sum())} of {len(range_table)}, Kruskal-Wallis "
      f"{int((range_table.kruskal_wallis_p < 0.05).sum())} of {len(range_table)}); p from {tests.min():.2g} to {tests.max():.2g}")
print(f"Mann-Whitney p {range_table.mann_whitney_p.min():.3f} to {range_table.mann_whitney_p.max():.3f}; "
      f"Kruskal-Wallis p {range_table.kruskal_wallis_p.min():.4f} to {range_table.kruskal_wallis_p.max():.4f}")
print("Median gridness of grid cells, range over readings:",
      {l: f"{range_table[f'median {l}'].min():.2f} to {range_table[f'median {l}'].max():.2f}" for l in LAYERS})
# Where the Kruskal-Wallis difference lies: two-sided Mann-Whitney tests between pairs of layers. These are
# not the criterion's tests, are uncorrected, and do not decide the outcome.
print("\nPairs of layers, Mann-Whitney (not the criterion's tests, uncorrected), readings with p < 0.05 and p range:")
for x, y in combinations(LAYERS, 2):
    p = range_table[f"pair {x}-{y} p"]
    print(f"  {x} against {y}: {int((p < 0.05).sum())} of {len(p)}, p {p.min():.2g} to {p.max():.2g}; median {x} above median {y} "
          f"in {int((range_table[f'median {x}'] > range_table[f'median {y}']).sum())}")
found = tests < 0.05
print("Outcome:", "not_reproduced" if found.all() else "methods_underspecified" if found.any() else "reproduced")
# Variant that does not decide the outcome: each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once.
rt = range_tests(once)
print(f"Variant, each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once: Mann-Whitney finds a difference in "
      f"{int((rt.mann_whitney_p < 0.05).sum())} of {len(rt)} (p {rt.mann_whitney_p.min():.3f} to {rt.mann_whitney_p.max():.3f}), "
      f"Kruskal-Wallis in {int((rt.kruskal_wallis_p < 0.05).sum())} of {len(rt)} (p {rt.kruskal_wallis_p.min():.4f} to {rt.kruskal_wallis_p.max():.4f})")

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified. The two tests the criterion names disagree. The Mann-Whitney test of layer II against the deeper layers finds a difference under 8 of the 56 readings (p 0.009 to 0.993), while the Kruskal-Wallis test across the four layers finds one under 53 of 56 (p 0.0001 to 0.159). The median gridness of grid cells is 0.42 to 0.78 in layer III, 0.23 to 0.58 in layer II, 0.28 to 0.53 in layer VI and 0.17 to 0.47 in layer V, and the layer III median is above the layer II median under all 56 readings. Pairwise Mann-Whitney tests, which are not the criterion's tests and are uncorrected, find layer II different from layer III under 46 of 56 readings, layer III from layer V under 49 and from layer VI under 25, but layer II from layer V under 2 and from layer VI under none. So the Kruskal-Wallis difference comes mostly from layer III, whose grid cells have higher gridness than those of layer II as well as those of layers V and VI; pooling layer III with layers V and VI hides this from the Mann-Whitney test. The ranges themselves are alike: in every layer they run from about 0 to between 1.14 and 1.49. With the radius reading added the tests still disagree (2 of 32 and 32 of 32 before). Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, the Mann-Whitney test finds a difference under 3 of 56 readings and the Kruskal-Wallis test under 10 of 56, so the tests still disagree.

Claim grid-stable¶

All 203 grid cells had stable periodic firing patterns within and between trials.

Criterion: grid cells as in layer2-grid. Between trials, for cells recorded in two trials (the 20-minute files): (a) a positive map correlation with Pearson p < 0.05, or (b) gridness above 0 in each trial's map. Within a trial: the same tests on the maps of (a) the first and second halves, (b) odd and even minutes, of each trial. Reproduced when every grid cell passes under every reading; partially reproduced when at least 90% do; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. A cell passes a combination when it passes the within-trial reading in each of its trials and, if it was recorded in two trials, the between-trial reading. Under O1 (b) only the first trial is used within trials.

In [14]:
def stability(frame, T, G):
    bname, rest = G.split("|", 1)
    g = frame[sg.classify(frame, T, G, 0.05).grid]
    within_tests = {}
    for split, test in product(("halves", "minutes"), ("correlation", "gridness")):
        ok = pd.Series(True, index=g.index)
        for k in ([0] if T == "first" else [0, 1]):
            has = g.trials > k
            if test == "correlation":
                passed = (g[f"within|{k}|{split}|{bname}|r"] > 0) & (g[f"within|{k}|{split}|{bname}|p"] < 0.05)
            else:
                passed = (g[f"within|{k}|{split}|{bname}|0|{rest}"] > 0) & (g[f"within|{k}|{split}|{bname}|1|{rest}"] > 0)
            ok &= passed | ~has
        within_tests[(split, test)] = ok
    two = g.trials == 2
    between_tests = {
        "correlation": (g[f"between|{bname}|r"] > 0) & (g[f"between|{bname}|p"] < 0.05),
        "gridness": (g[f"grid|first|{G}"] > 0) & (g[f"between|{bname}|trial2|{rest}"] > 0),
    }
    rows = []
    for (split, wt), w in within_tests.items():
        for bt, b in between_tests.items():
            stable = w & (b | ~two)
            rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, within=f"{split}, {wt}", between=bt, grid_cells=len(g),
                             two_trial_cells=int(two.sum()), within_pass=w.mean(),
                             between_pass=b[two].mean() if two.any() else np.nan,
                             stable=stable.mean()))
    return rows

Claims spacing-dorsoventral and fieldsize-dorsoventral: blocked¶

Both need each recording site's distance from the postrhinal border, measured in the histology (SOM, Histology; fig. S3). The units table has depth ("the depth of the inserted electrodes in meters"), the depth the tetrodes were lowered to, which is not that distance, and no other column or file gives it; the electrodes table has one row per file, location "MEC", with no coordinates (data check). Both claims are blocked with data_missing.

Claim grid-phase-orientation¶

In all layers the spatial phase of nearby grid cells was distributed (their vertices were offset), while grid orientation was consistent across simultaneously recorded cells.

Criterion: pairs of grid cells recorded together (same file and trial). Orientation, compared modulo 60 degrees, is consistent when the within-file pairwise differences are smaller than those between files of different rats, by a one-sided Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05 (a standard choice named in the claim). The pairs of different rats are taken (a) within the same layer, (b) from all layers (readings, as answered). Phase is distributed when for more than half the pairs the peak of the rate-map crosscorrelogram nearest the centre is displaced from the centre by (a) more than a fifth of the grid spacing (the mean of the two cells'), (b) more than the 3 cm bin. Reproduced when both parts hold under every reading, readings O1 to O3 included, in each layer with at least one simultaneous pair. As the criterion judges each layer, pairs are of cells of the same layer; pairs of cells of different layers are counted below and left out. The criterion names no outcome but reproduced, and the claims file's rule for readings applies: a claim that holds under some readings and not under others is methods_underspecified.

In [15]:
def phase_orientation(T, G, frame=known):
    bname, _, _, loc, _ = G.split("|")
    g = frame[sg.classify(frame, T, G, 0.05).grid]
    info = g.set_index(["path", "unit"])[[f"orientation|{T}|{bname}|{loc}", f"spacing|{T}|{bname}|{loc}", "layer", "subject"]]
    info.columns = ["orientation", "spacing", "layer", "subject"]
    p = pairs.join(info.add_suffix("_a"), on=["path", "unit_a"], how="inner").join(info.add_suffix("_b"), on=["path", "unit_b"], how="inner")
    p = p[p.layer_a == p.layer_b]
    d = np.abs(p.orientation_a - p.orientation_b) % 60
    p = p.assign(d_orient=np.minimum(d, 60 - d), offset=p[f"offset|{T}|{bname}|{loc}"],
                 fifth=(p.spacing_a + p.spacing_b) / 2 / 5)
    rows = []
    for l in LAYERS:
        q = p[p.layer_a == l]
        if len(q) == 0:
            continue
        between = {}
        for pool, cl in (("layer", g[g.layer == l]), ("all layers", g)):
            o = cl[f"orientation|{T}|{bname}|{loc}"].to_numpy() % 60
            s = cl.subject.to_numpy()
            i, j = np.triu_indices(len(cl), 1)
            dd = np.abs(o[i] - o[j])[s[i] != s[j]]
            between[pool] = np.minimum(dd, 60 - dd)
        p_of = {pool: stats.mannwhitneyu(q.d_orient, b, alternative="less").pvalue if len(b) else np.nan
                for pool, b in between.items()}
        rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, layer=l, pairs=len(q), files=q.path.nunique(), rats=q.subject.nunique(),
                         median_within=q.d_orient.median(), median_between_rats=np.median(between["layer"]),
                         orientation_p=p_of["layer"], orientation_p_all_layers=p_of["all layers"],
                         displaced_fifth=(q.offset > q.fifth).mean(), displaced_3cm=(q.offset > 3).mean(),
                         no_peak=int(q.offset.isna().sum())))
    return rows

                              orientation_p_min=("orientation_p", "min"), orientation_p_max=("orientation_p", "max"),

                              displaced_3cm_min=("displaced_3cm", "min"), displaced_3cm_max=("displaced_3cm", "max"),

def judge_readings(po):
    rows = []
    for (T, G), x in po.groupby(["trials", "gridness"]):
        for pool, col in (("same layer", "orientation_holds"), ("all layers", "orientation_holds_all_layers")):
            for phase in ("phase_fifth", "phase_3cm"):
                rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, pool=pool, phase=phase, both_every_layer=bool((x[col] & x[phase]).all()),
                                 phase_every_layer=bool(x[phase].all()),
                                 orientation_layers=",".join(x[x[col]].layer), orientation_fails=",".join(x[~x[col]].layer)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified. The phase part holds in every layer under every reading: 75% to 98.5% of simultaneous pairs have the crosscorrelogram peak nearest the centre displaced by more than a fifth of the spacing, and 92.6% to 100% by more than 3 cm. Orientation is more alike within files than between rats in layers II and III under every reading (p below 0.001), but not under every reading in layers V (p up to 0.50 with the layer's own rats and 0.52 with all layers; holds under 42 and 41 of 56 readings) and VI (p up to 0.34 and 0.50; 35 and 23 of 56), which come from three rats each. Both parts hold in every layer under 90 of the 224 readings (26 of 56 with the layer's own rats and 19 of 56 with all layers, under each phase reading), and not under the other 134. These counts rest on p-values near 0.05, and runs of the same code on other machines have differed from them by a reading or two (not run here); the outcome does not depend on them. The criterion names no outcome for this case, so the claims file's rule applies and the readings' disagreement blocks the claim. 20 of the 487 simultaneous grid pairs of the first reading pair cells of different layers and are not counted.

The previous version called this claim partially reproduced, an outcome the criterion does not name; the verifier pointed this out, and the outcome is now the one the claims file's rule gives. It is the outcome this claim had before the answer, for the same reason.

Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, the phase part still holds in every layer under every reading, orientation holds under 56, 47, 43 and 38 of 56 readings in layers II, III, V and VI with the layer's own rats (56, 54, 39 and 21 with all layers), and both parts hold in every layer under 66 of 224 readings, so the readings still disagree.

Claim hd-layers¶

No head-direction cells were found in layer II, whereas a large proportion of the cells in layers III to VI had directional preferences (273 of 385 cells, counting conjunctive cells).

Criterion: cells of two-LED files only; head-direction cells by the SOM criteria (Watson U2 significant and the odd/even-minute correlation significant) with readings O1 and O4; directional cells are head-direction plus conjunctive cells. Reproduced when no layer II cell passes and the fractions are within tolerance (deeper 0.709 +/- 0.071; III 0.669 +/- 0.067; V 0.878 +/- 0.088; VI 0.669 +/- 0.067); partially reproduced when no layer II cell passes and the deeper fraction is above 0.5 but a number is outside tolerance. The dandiset holds the non-grid cells too (data check), so the fractions can be formed.

EXPECTED_HD = {"III to VI": (0.709, 0.071), "III": (0.669, 0.067), "V": (0.878, 0.088), "VI": (0.669, 0.067)}

for T, _, a in sg.readings(with_grid=False):
    hd = sg.classify(tracked, T, sg.GRID_READINGS[0], a).hd
    frac = {l: hd[tracked.layer == l].mean() for l in LAYERS}
    frac["III to VI"] = hd[tracked.layer != "II"].mean()
    n_ii = int(hd[tracked.layer == "II"].sum())
    tol = all(within(frac[k], *EXPECTED_HD[k]) for k in EXPECTED_HD)
    rows.append(dict(trials=T, level=a, layer_II=f"{n_ii}/{(tracked.layer == 'II').sum()}",
                     **{k: frac[k] for k in ["III to VI", "III", "V", "VI"]},

Result: not reproduced. Under every reading some layer II cells pass both head-direction criteria: 9, 7, 4 and 2 of 43. All of them are from rat 11265, in its two 20-minute files of 16 March 2006 (16030601 and 16030604), and their U2 (0.36 to 9.8) is below the median of the deeper head-direction cells (13.1). Watson's U2 alone is significant for 39 to 41 of the 43 layer II cells, so the block correlation decides which pass. In the deeper layers 0.671 to 0.733 of cells are directional, within 0.709 +/- 0.071, and layer V (0.924 to 0.937) is within its range; layer III (0.527 to 0.599) is below its range under every reading and layer VI (0.713 to 0.790) above it under two of four. The claim needs no layer II cell to pass even for a partial reproduction.

The two files show no sign of bad tracking: their median LED separation, 3.7 and 3.9 cm, ranks 4th and 6th smallest of the 71 two-LED files, and fewer than 0.05% of their samples have the LEDs more than 15 cm apart. They are the only two files whose positions span 150 cm. Without them no layer II cell passes (0 of 17) and the deeper fractions are unchanged, which would be partially reproduced; this variant selects files after seeing the result and does not decide the outcome. It is also weaker than its count suggests: the 17 layer II cells left are all from rat 11278, and 11 of them are in sub-11278_ses-31080502, one of the two files whose LEDs are more than 15 cm apart in most samples. Leaving out that file as well, 0 of 6 layer II cells pass, so the "none" of this variant rests on 6 layer II cells with plausible tracking. Leaving out the two files with LEDs more than 15 cm apart in most samples (13 layer III and 11 layer II cells) changes nothing in layer II (9, 7, 4 and 2 of 32), and counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once leaves 9, 7, 4 and 2 of 26.

Claim hd-with-grid-colocalized¶

Beneath layer II, head-direction cells were usually recorded together with grid cells.

Criterion: two-LED files, layers III to VI, cell classes as in hd-layers and layer2-grid. The unit of colocalization is (a) the file (one recording), (b) the tetrode within a file. The head-direction cells are the pure head-direction cells of table S1B, and the cell found with them is another cell of the unit: (a) a pure grid cell, (b) a grid or conjunctive cell (readings, as answered). Reproduced when, under every reading, more than half of the units holding a head-direction cell also hold such a cell; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

In [19]:
deep = tracked[tracked.layer.isin(DEEP)]
deep_once = deep[first_copy.reindex(deep.index)]       # each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, for variants


def coloc_of(cells_):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(cells_, T, G, a)
        for companion, other in (("pure grid", c.grid & ~c.hd), ("grid or conjunctive", c.grid)):
            frame = cells_.assign(pure_hd=c.pure_hd, other=other)
            for unit_name, keys in (("file", ["path"]), ("tetrode", ["path", "tetrode"])):
                g = frame.groupby(keys).agg(hd=("pure_hd", "any"), other=("other", "any"))
                with_hd = g[g.hd]
                rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, companion=companion, unit=unit_name, units_with_hd=len(with_hd),
                                 also_grid=int(with_hd.other.sum()), fraction=with_hd.other.mean()))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out["more_than_half"] = out.fraction > 0.5
    return out


coloc = coloc_of(deep)
print(coloc.groupby(["companion", "unit"]).agg(units_min=("units_with_hd", "min"), units_max=("units_with_hd", "max"),
                                  fraction_min=("fraction", "min"), fraction_median=("fraction", "median"),
                                  fraction_max=("fraction", "max")).round(3).to_string())
print(coloc[(coloc.trials == READING[0]) & (coloc.gridness == READING[1]) & (coloc.level == READING[2])].round(3).to_string())
print(f"\nReadings (trials, gridness, level, companion, unit) with more than half: {int(coloc.more_than_half.sum())} of {len(coloc)}")
print(coloc.groupby(["companion", "unit"]).more_than_half.agg(["sum", "size"]).to_string())
print("Outcome:", outcome_of(np.where(coloc.more_than_half, "reproduced", "not_reproduced")))
# Variant that does not decide the outcome: each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once.
coloc_once = coloc_of(deep_once)
print("Variant, each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, readings with more than half:")
print(coloc_once.groupby(["companion", "unit"]).agg(units_min=("units_with_hd", "min"), units_max=("units_with_hd", "max"),
                                                   fraction_min=("fraction", "min"), fraction_max=("fraction", "max"),
                                                   more_than_half=("more_than_half", "sum"), readings=("more_than_half", "size")).round(3).to_string())
print("  outcome:", outcome_of(np.where(coloc_once.more_than_half, "reproduced", "not_reproduced")))

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified. Counted by file, 75% to 91% of the 49 to 57 files with a pure head-direction cell in layers III to VI also hold a grid or conjunctive cell, and 47% to 60% hold a pure grid cell (more than half under 83 of 112 readings). Counted by tetrode, 36% to 48% of 107 to 128 tetrodes hold a grid or conjunctive cell, and 14.5% to 19.4% a pure grid cell, below half under every reading. The readings disagree. The answer confirmed the pure head-direction cells and another cell, which this attempt had used, and added the pure grid cell as a reading; it lowers the fractions but does not change the outcome.

Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, by file 67% to 84% of the 42 to 47 files hold a grid or conjunctive cell (more than half under all 112 readings) and 30% to 48% a pure grid cell (under none); by tetrode both are below half under every reading. The readings still disagree.

Claim hd-tuning-breadth-layers¶

The breadth of directional tuning did not differ between layers III, V and VI (mean U2 18.2, 25.2 and 18.3; mean angular standard deviation 55.9, 52.2 and 58.2 degrees; P > 0.05).

Criterion: a claim of absence; tests (a) one-way ANOVA, (b) Kruskal-Wallis, each on U2 and on the angular standard deviation; cells (a) pure head-direction cells, (b) with conjunctive cells. The angular standard deviation is (a) Batschelet's angular deviation, sqrt(2(1 - r)), (b) his circular standard deviation, sqrt(-2 ln r) (readings, as answered). Reproduced when no reading finds a difference at p < 0.05; not reproduced when all do; methods_underspecified when they disagree; a reproduced absence with means outside tolerance is partially reproduced.

In [20]:
EXPECTED_U2 = {"III": (18.2, 1.82), "V": (25.2, 2.52), "VI": (18.3, 1.83)}
EXPECTED_ASD = {"III": (55.9, 5.59), "V": (52.2, 5.22), "VI": (58.2, 5.82)}
def breadth_of(cells_):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(cells_, T, G, a)
        for cell_reading, sel in (("pure head-direction", c.pure_hd), ("with conjunctive", c.hd)):
            if cell_reading == "with conjunctive" and G != sg.GRID_READINGS[0]:
                continue          # does not depend on the gridness reading
            g = cells_[sel]
            for measure, col, exp in (("U2", f"u2|{T}", EXPECTED_U2), ("angular deviation", f"ang_dev|{T}", EXPECTED_ASD),
                                      ("circular sd", f"circ_sd|{T}", EXPECTED_ASD)):
                groups = [g[g.layer == l][col] for l in DEEP]
                means = {l: x.mean() for l, x in zip(DEEP, groups)}
                rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G if cell_reading.startswith("pure") else "any", level=a, cells=cell_reading,
                                 measure=measure, **{f"n {l}": len(x) for l, x in zip(DEEP, groups)},
                                 **{f"mean {l}": means[l] for l in DEEP},
                                 anova_p=stats.f_oneway(*groups).pvalue, kruskal_p=stats.kruskal(*groups).pvalue,
                                 means_in_tolerance=all(within(means[l], *exp[l]) for l in DEEP)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


breadth = breadth_of(deep)
print(breadth.groupby(["cells", "measure"]).agg(
    readings=("anova_p", "size"), anova_p_min=("anova_p", "min"), anova_p_max=("anova_p", "max"),
    kruskal_p_min=("kruskal_p", "min"), kruskal_p_max=("kruskal_p", "max"),

The readings still disagree, though the differences are much rarer when repeated cells are left out.

Claim hd-full-range¶

The entire range of head directions was represented by the preferred directions of head-direction cells in each of layers III, V and VI.

Criterion: head-direction and conjunctive cells of each layer; preferred direction is the bin of peak rate. Reproduced when each (a) 30-degree, (b) 60-degree, (c) 90-degree sector holds the preferred direction of at least one cell of the layer, in all three layers; not reproduced when no reading holds in some layer; otherwise methods_underspecified. Sectors start at 0 degrees of the camera's frame (a standard choice).

Claim hd-colocalized-distributed¶

Preferred directions of simultaneously recorded head-direction cells in the same area were widely distributed; in most ensembles of five or more cells (8 of 12) they showed no significant clustering.

Criterion: every file with 5 or more simultaneously recorded head-direction cells; the directions of the cells' mean vectors tested for clustering with Watson's one-sample U2 test of uniformity at p < 0.05, against the critical value for the number of cells (Stephens' small-sample form, which gives the paper's 0.177 to 0.182 for 5 to 15 cells). Cells (a) pure head-direction cells, (b) with conjunctive cells. Reproduced when, under a reading, fewer than half of the ensembles show clustering; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. Expected 4 +/- 0.4 clustered of 12 +/- 1.2 ensembles.

Claim hd-stable-trials¶

Directional tuning curves were always stable across the two trials (circular correlation r = 0.84, P < 0.001).

Criterion: head-direction and conjunctive cells recorded in both trials (the 20-minute two-LED files). Readings: (a) across cells, the circular-circular correlation of the preferred direction in trial 1 with that in trial 2 (Jammalamadaka's coefficient, a standard choice); (b) per cell, the Pearson correlation of the two trials' 60-bin tuning curves, averaged over cells, its mean tested against 0 by a one-sample t-test. Reproduced when, under a reading, r is within 0.84 +/- 0.084 with p < 0.001; methods_underspecified when one reading reproduces and another fails.

In [23]:
two_trial = deep[deep.trials == 2]


def stable_of(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, _, a in sg.readings(with_grid=False):
        g = frame[sg.classify(frame, T, sg.GRID_READINGS[0], a).hd]
        silent = g["trial_peak_dir|0"].isna() | g["trial_peak_dir|1"].isna()
        g = g[~silent]
        rcc, pcc = sg.circular_correlation(g["trial_peak_dir|0"].to_numpy(float), g["trial_peak_dir|1"].to_numpy(float))
        per_cell = []
        for t0, t1 in zip(g["trial_tuning|0"], g["trial_tuning|1"]):
            ok = ~np.isnan(t0) & ~np.isnan(t1)
            per_cell.append(stats.pearsonr(t0[ok], t1[ok])[0])
        per_cell = np.array(per_cell)
        rows.append(dict(trials=T, level=a, cells=len(g), dropped_silent_in_a_trial=int(silent.sum()),
                         files=g.path.nunique(), rats=g.subject.nunique(),
                         circular_r=rcc, circular_p=pcc, mean_curve_r=per_cell.mean(),
                         curve_r_range=f"{per_cell.min():.2f} to {per_cell.max():.2f}",
                         t_test_p=stats.ttest_1samp(per_cell, 0).pvalue,
                         cells_with_curve_r_below_0_5=int((per_cell < 0.5).sum())))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out["a_reproduces"] = out.circular_r.between(0.756, 0.924) & (out.circular_p < 0.001)
    out["b_reproduces"] = out.mean_curve_r.between(0.756, 0.924) & (out.t_test_p < 0.001)
    return out

Result: reproduced. For the 88 to 96 head-direction and conjunctive cells in the 19 or 20 two-trial files (3 rats), the circular correlation of the preferred direction between trials is 0.78 to 0.85 and the mean correlation of the two trials' tuning curves 0.77 to 0.81, all with p below 0.001 and within 0.84 +/- 0.084, under both readings and all four classifications. The statement's "always" holds less well: 7 to 14 of these cells have tuning curves correlated below 0.5 between trials. Two cells silent in one trial are left out under each reading.

The third two-LED file with questionable LED geometry, sub-11025_ses-06050501 (LEDs more than 15 cm apart in 17.8% of samples), holds no head-direction or conjunctive cell under the pooled readings and 2 and 1 under the first-trial readings, whose preferred directions change by 180 and 54 degrees between trials. Without that file the tuning-curve reading still holds under all four readings (0.771 to 0.815), but the circular correlation falls to 0.538 and 0.645 under the first-trial readings, outside 0.84 +/- 0.084, although the cells left out are unstable ones. The circular correlation is centred on the circular means of the preferred directions, which fill the circle (hd-full-range), so leaving out one or two cells can move it far. Under this variant the readings would disagree; the criterion leaves no file out, so the variant does not decide the outcome, but it shows that the circular-correlation reading is fragile here. Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once (72 to 78 cells), the circular correlation is 0.841 to 0.897 and the mean curve correlation 0.775 to 0.812, which reproduces under both readings.

Claim hd-rates¶

In head-direction cells, firing rose from a low background rate (typically below 0.5 Hz) to a high maximum rate (5 to 40 Hz) when the rat's head faced the cell's range of directions.

Criterion: head-direction cells of the two-LED files, (a) pure, (b) with conjunctive cells. Peak rate: the highest bin of the unsmoothed 60-bin tuning curve. Background rate: (a) the lowest bin, (b) the mean over the bins more than 90 degrees from the preferred direction; "typically" is the median over cells. Reproduced when, under a reading, the median background rate is below 0.55 Hz and at least 90% of cells have peak rates from 4.5 to 44 Hz; methods_underspecified when readings disagree.

In [24]:
def rates_of(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(frame, T, G, a)
        for cell_reading, sel in (("pure head-direction", c.pure_hd), ("with conjunctive", c.hd)):
            if cell_reading == "with conjunctive" and G != sg.GRID_READINGS[0]:
                continue
            g = frame[sel]
            peak_ok = g[f"peak_rate|{T}"].between(4.5, 44).mean()
            for bg in ("bg_min", "bg_far"):
                med = g[f"{bg}|{T}"].median()
                rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G if cell_reading.startswith("pure") else "any", level=a, cells=cell_reading,
                                 background="lowest bin" if bg == "bg_min" else "beyond 90 deg", n=len(g),
                                 median_background=med, peak_in_range=peak_ok,
                                 median_peak=g[f"peak_rate|{T}"].median(),
                                 reproduces=(med < 0.55) and (peak_ok >= 0.9)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: not reproduced. The background rate is low as stated: its median over cells is 0 Hz in the lowest bin and 0.32 to 0.50 Hz beyond 90 degrees of the preferred direction, below 0.55 Hz under every reading. But only 65.5% to 71.2% of head-direction cells peak between 4.5 and 44 Hz, where the criterion needs 90%; the median peak is 5.9 to 6.9 Hz, and 34% of cells (first reading, with conjunctive cells) peak below 4.5 Hz.

Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, 63.6% to 70.1% of head-direction cells peak between 4.5 and 44 Hz, and the claim is not reproduced under any reading.

Claim deep-hd-conjunctive¶

The proportion of grid cells with conjunctive head-direction tuning depended on layer (66% in layer III, 90% in layer V, 28% in layer VI, none in layer II); the difference was significant across all four layers and across layers III to VI.

Criterion: two-LED files; grid and conjunctive cells by the SOM, readings O1 to O4. Chi-square readings: (a) conjunctive against non-conjunctive grid cells per layer; (b) conjunctive cells against all other cells per layer. Reproduced when, under a reading, both tests are significant (p < 0.001 for four layers, p < 0.05 for III to VI) and the four fractions are within tolerance (0, 0.66 +/- 0.066, 0.90 +/- 0.09, 0.28 +/- 0.028); partially reproduced when no layer II cell is conjunctive and the four-layer test is significant but a fraction or the three-layer test fails.

Result: not reproduced. Layer II has conjunctive cells under every reading (1 to 8, all from rat 11265, 0.04 to 0.32 of layer II grid cells), and the claim needs none even for a partial reproduction. The conjunctive fraction of grid cells is 0.86 to 0.95 in layer V, within 0.90 +/- 0.09, but 0.46 to 0.59 in layer III (paper 0.66) and 0.53 to 0.74 in layer VI (paper 0.28). The four-layer chi-square has p from 1.9e-11 to 0.23 and the three-layer one from 1.6e-05 to 0.78, depending on the reading. The radius reading added by the answer changes none of this.

The layer II conjunctive cells are in the two 150-cm files of rat 11265 discussed under hd-layers. Without those files layer II has none. The four-layer chi-square then has p 2.4e-07 to 0.00033 under reading (a), below 0.001 under all 112 readings, but 0.00014 to 0.054 under reading (b), below 0.001 under only 8 of 112. So that variant would be partially reproduced under reading (a) and not reproduced under most readings of (b): its readings disagree, and it would be methods_underspecified, not partially reproduced. Leaving out also the two files with implausible LED geometry, p is 3.6e-05 to 0.034 under (a) (below 0.001 under 60 of 112) and 0.00079 to 0.34 under (b) (1 of 112). Like the variant under hd-layers, these select files after seeing the result and do not decide the outcome. Leaving out only the two files with implausible LED geometry, or counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, leaves 1 to 8 layer II conjunctive cells.

The earlier attempt called this claim reproduced. Its claim was the abstract's sentence, that grid, head-direction and conjunctive cells occur together in the deeper layers, which the data still show (table S1B above). The claim now carries the paper's per-layer fractions and requires no conjunctive cell in layer II, and the data meet neither.

Claim gridness-hd-continuous¶

Grid cells and head-direction cells formed overlapping populations; the joint distribution of gridness and directional tuning was continuous, with some grid cells directionally tuned and some head-direction cells having grid structure.

Criterion: two-LED cells, gridness against Watson U2 (log scale) as in Fig. 3E. Reproduced when conjunctive cells exist and, under readings O1 to O4, the cells passing either criterion form no separate clusters, read as no gap along either axis wider than a quarter of that axis's range among them (a standard choice).

In [28]:
def continuity_of(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(frame, T, G, a)
        either = frame[c.grid | c.hd]
        row = dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, conjunctive=int(c.conj.sum()), cells=len(either))
        for axis, values in (("gridness", either[f"grid|{T}|{G}"].dropna()), ("log10 U2", np.log10(either[f"u2|{T}"].dropna()))):
            v = np.sort(values.to_numpy())
            gap = np.diff(v).max() / (v[-1] - v[0])
            row[f"largest gap, {axis} (fraction of range)"] = gap
        rows.append(row)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out["continuous"] = (out.conjunctive > 0) & (out.filter(like="largest gap").max(axis=1) <= 0.25)
    return out


cont = continuity_of(tracked)
print(cont.describe().round(3).to_string())

Claim conj-tuning-similar¶

Directional tuning of conjunctive cells did not differ from that of pure head-direction cells (mean U2 18.0 against 19.4, P > 0.05).

Criterion: a claim of absence; (a) two-sided t-test, (b) two-sided Mann-Whitney test of U2, conjunctive against pure head-direction cells, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when no reading finds a difference; not reproduced when all do; methods_underspecified when they disagree; a reproduced absence with means outside tolerance (18.0 +/- 1.8, 19.4 +/- 1.94) is partially reproduced. All two-LED cells are used, as the paper's 53 and 220 cells span all layers.

In [29]:
def conj_u2_of(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(frame, T, G, a)
        x, y = frame[c.conj][f"u2|{T}"], frame[c.pure_hd][f"u2|{T}"]
        rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, conjunctive=len(x), pure_hd=len(y), mean_conj=x.mean(), mean_hd=y.mean(),
                         median_conj=x.median(), median_hd=y.median(), t_p=stats.ttest_ind(x, y).pvalue,
                         mw_p=stats.mannwhitneyu(x, y, alternative="two-sided").pvalue))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Variant, each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once: t-tests finding a difference 71 of 112, Mann-Whitney 26 of 112

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified. The t-test finds a difference in U2 between conjunctive and pure head-direction cells under 98 of 112 readings (mean U2 12.0 to 19.4 against 18.2 to 25.4), the Mann-Whitney test under 42 of 112 (medians 8.8 to 15.5 against 10.5 to 17.4). The means are within tolerance under 3 of 112 readings.

Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, the t-test finds a difference under 71 of 112 readings and the Mann-Whitney test under 26, so the tests still disagree.

Claim cue-rotation-coherent: blocked¶

The claim needs the cue-rotation trials of five rats in the small circular box, and the position of the cue card in each. No file names its enclosure, its condition or a cue rotation, and there is no trial table; the description says only that the rat ran in a 1 x 1 m enclosure. The small circle is not there in another guise either: every circular file spans 200 cm (data check). The rotated trials cannot be found, so the claim is blocked with data_missing.

Claim speed¶

Regression showed a consistent positive speed-rate relation in nearly all grid cells (141 of 150), head-direction cells (153 of 220) and conjunctive cells (45 of 53).

Criterion: per cell, firing rate in 1-s bins regressed on speed over the trial, all bins kept. Counting: (a) slope positive with P < 0.001; (b) slope positive, the count then tested against half by a one-sided binomial sign test at p < 0.001. Grid cells are the grid cells that are not conjunctive, from all rats; head-direction (pure) and conjunctive cells from two-LED files. Speed from (a) path length, (b) displacement over the bin; positions (a) smoothed, (b) raw; trials as O1; significance from (a) the slope, (b) Pearson's r (the same test as the slope for a simple regression), (c) Spearman's rank correlation. As answered, the counting and significance readings are readings of the reported number, and for each combination of method details (speed measure, positions, trials and cell classes) the best of them is taken: reproduced when under one of them all three fractions are within tolerance (0.94 +/- 0.094, 0.695 +/- 0.070, 0.849 +/- 0.085); partially reproduced when none does but under one the grid and conjunctive fractions exceed the head-direction fraction and all exceed one half. The claim takes that outcome when every combination of method details gives it; methods_underspecified when they disagree.

EXPECTED_SPEED = {"grid_only": (0.94, 0.094), "pure_hd": (0.695, 0.070), "conj": (0.849, 0.085)}
def speed_table_of(frame):
    rows = []
    for T, G, a in sg.readings():
        c = sg.classify(frame, T, G, a)
        for sr in sg.SPEED_READINGS:
            slope = frame[f"slope|{T}|{sr}"]
            for count, sig in (("P < 0.001, slope", f"p_linear|{T}|{sr}"), ("P < 0.001, Spearman", f"p_spearman|{T}|{sr}"),
                               ("positive slope", None)):
                passed = (slope > 0) & ((frame[sig] < 0.001) if sig else True)
                row = dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, speed=sr, count=count)
                for cls in EXPECTED_SPEED:
                    sel = c[cls]
                    row[f"{cls} n"] = int(sel.sum())
                    row[cls] = passed[sel].mean()
                    if sig is None:
                        row[f"{cls} sign p"] = stats.binomtest(int(passed[sel].sum()), int(sel.sum()), 0.5, alternative="greater").pvalue
                tol = all(within(row[k], *v) for k, v in EXPECTED_SPEED.items())
                order = row["grid_only"] > row["pure_hd"] and row["conj"] > row["pure_hd"] and min(row[k] for k in EXPECTED_SPEED) > 0.5
                # under the positive-slope count, the count of each class must also pass the sign test at p < 0.001
                sign_ok = sig is not None or all(row[f"{k} sign p"] < 0.001 for k in EXPECTED_SPEED)
                row["sign_test_ok"] = sign_ok
                row["outcome without the sign test"] = "reproduced" if tol else "partially_reproduced" if order else "not_reproduced"
                row["outcome"] = row["outcome without the sign test"] if sign_ok else "not_reproduced"
                rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Correlation of rate with speed per cell (median by class): {'conjunctive': 0.052, 'grid': 0.078, 'head direction': 0.05}
Slopes -0.352 to 0.241 Hz per cm/s; outside the axes: 1

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified. Counted as cells with a positive slope at P < 0.001, 0.129 to 0.446 of grid cells, 0.094 to 0.282 of head-direction cells and 0.081 to 0.415 of conjunctive cells pass, against 0.94, 0.695 and 0.849, under every combination of readings. Counted by a positive slope, 0.815 to 0.886 of grid cells, 0.622 to 0.708 of head-direction cells and 0.686 to 0.822 of conjunctive cells pass. Under that count the criterion also asks that each class's count pass a one-sided sign test against half at p < 0.001; the head-direction count fails it in 2 of the 448 positive-slope rows (largest p 0.0015), which are then not reproduced. Taking the best reading of the number for each of the 448 combinations of method details, 119 give reproduced (all three fractions within tolerance), 325 partially reproduced (the order holds) and 4 not reproduced. The combinations disagree, so the claim is methods_underspecified. Without the sign test the split is 119, 327 and 2, as in the previous version, which computed the test but did not apply it. Reproduced combinations are most frequent with path-length speeds and the first trial (37 and 33 of 56) and rare with displacement speeds (2 to 11 of 56). Counting each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) once, the best reading per combination gives 125 reproduced, 201 partially reproduced and 122 not reproduced, so the method details still disagree.

The question asked how to read the criterion, which called the claim reproduced "under a combination of readings" and also methods_underspecified "when readings disagree". The answer separates readings of the number, of which the best counts, from method details, which must agree. The outcome is the same as before the answer, now for a stated reason: the method details disagree.

The earlier attempt called this claim reproduced from a different measure (the correlation of rate with speed over 5 cm/s bins, against shuffled spike trains) and a different claim (the abstract's "all cell types were modulated by running speed").

Claim speed-slope-steeper¶

The slope of the speed-rate regression was steeper for conjunctive cells and grid cells than for head-direction cells, and did not differ between conjunctive and grid cells.

Criterion: slopes from the speed claim's regressions, its readings; one-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD. Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.005, Tukey gives conjunctive and grid each steeper than head-direction at p < 0.05, and conjunctive against grid p > 0.05; partially reproduced when the ANOVA is significant at p < 0.05 and one of the two comparisons with head-direction is.

rows = []
for T, G, a in sg.readings():
    c = sg.classify(known, T, G, a)
    for sr in sg.SPEED_READINGS:
        col = f"slope|{T}|{sr}"
        g, h, j = known[c.grid_only][col], known[c.pure_hd][col], known[c.conj][col]
        anova = stats.f_oneway(g, h, j)
        tukey = stats.tukey_hsd(g, h, j).pvalue
        conj_hd = tukey[2, 1] < 0.05 and j.mean() > h.mean()
        grid_hd = tukey[0, 1] < 0.05 and g.mean() > h.mean()
        outcome = ("reproduced" if anova.pvalue < 0.005 and conj_hd and grid_hd and tukey[2, 0] > 0.05 else
                   "partially_reproduced" if anova.pvalue < 0.05 and (conj_hd or grid_hd) else "not_reproduced")
        rows.append(dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, speed=sr, df=f"F(2,{len(g) + len(h) + len(j) - 3})", F=anova.statistic,
                         anova_p=anova.pvalue, mean_grid=g.mean(), mean_hd=h.mean(), mean_conj=j.mean(),
                         tukey_conj_hd=tukey[2, 1], tukey_grid_hd=tukey[0, 1], tukey_conj_grid=tukey[2, 0], outcome=outcome))

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified, because it depends on speed. The analysis ran: under all 448 combinations the ANOVA is significant (F 4.5 to 13.6, p at most 0.012) and grid cells have steeper slopes than head-direction cells (Tukey p at most 0.0084), but conjunctive cells do not differ from head-direction cells (Tukey p 0.06 to 0.99), which on its own would make the claim partially reproduced under every reading. Conjunctive and grid cells differ under some readings (Tukey p 0.0004 to 0.29). The degrees of freedom are F(2,444) to F(2,488). The verifier would call this claim partially reproduced, on these numbers; it stays blocked because the claims file lists speed under its depends_on, and the protocol (Author, step 1.5) says that "a claim that depends on a blocked claim is blocked for the same reason". That is why blocked_by is methods_underspecified, the reason speed is blocked. The disagreement is recorded.

Claim speed-intercept¶

The intercept of the speed-rate regression was positive in all cells but one (422 of 423), and mean rates at the lowest speeds (0 to 3 cm/s) were about 2.3 to 2.5 Hz in each cell class, so firing persisted during brief stops.

Criterion: regressions and readings as in the speed claim. Averages: (a) the mean over cells of each cell's mean rate in the 1-s bins from 0 to 3 cm/s; (b) the mean over all such bins of the class pooled. Reproduced when, under a reading, the fraction is within 0.998 +/- 0.0998 and the rates within 2.26 +/- 0.03, 2.50 +/- 0.02 and 2.39 +/- 0.05 Hz; partially reproduced when the fraction holds and the rates are within 10% of the printed values.

EXPECTED_LOW = {"grid_only": 2.26, "pure_hd": 2.50, "conj": 2.39}
SPREAD_LOW = {"grid_only": 0.03, "pure_hd": 0.02, "conj": 0.05}
rows = []
for T, G, a in sg.readings():
    c = sg.classify(known, T, G, a)
    sel = c.grid_only | c.pure_hd | c.conj
    for sr in sg.SPEED_READINGS:
        positive = (known[f"intercept|{T}|{sr}"] > 0)[sel]
        for avg in ("mean of cells", "pooled bins"):
            row = dict(trials=T, gridness=G, level=a, speed=sr, average=avg, cells=int(sel.sum()),
                       positive_intercept=positive.mean(), negative=int((~positive).sum()))
            for k in EXPECTED_LOW:
                g = known[c[k]]
                if avg == "mean of cells":
                    row[k] = g[f"low_rate|{T}|{sr}"].mean()
                else:
                    row[k] = g[f"low_spikes|{T}|{sr}"].sum() / g[f"low_bins|{T}|{sr}"].sum()
            fraction_ok = within(row["positive_intercept"], 0.998, 0.0998)
            exact = all(within(row[k], EXPECTED_LOW[k], SPREAD_LOW[k]) for k in EXPECTED_LOW)
            ten = all(within(row[k], EXPECTED_LOW[k], 0.1 * EXPECTED_LOW[k]) for k in EXPECTED_LOW)
            row["outcome"] = ("reproduced" if fraction_ok and exact else
                              "partially_reproduced" if fraction_ok and ten else "not_reproduced")
            rows.append(row)

Result: blocked, methods_underspecified, because it depends on speed. The analysis ran: the intercept is positive in 98.2% to 99.8% of cells (at most 8 negative), within tolerance, but the mean rates at 0 to 3 cm/s are 1.2 to 1.9 Hz for grid cells, 1.1 to 1.8 Hz for head-direction cells and 0.9 to 1.6 Hz for conjunctive cells, more than 10% below the paper's 2.26, 2.50 and 2.39 Hz under every reading, which on its own would make the claim not reproduced. Speeds depend on the scale of the positions, which the files rescale (data check); the rescaling is about 11% in the 19 circular files. Taking in those files the bins up to 3 cm/s times 200/180, as if their positions were scaled to the SOM's 180 cm circle, the class means are 1.22 to 1.90, 1.18 to 1.76 and 0.93 to 1.53 Hz, and no row has all three within 10%; in the 120 cells of those files the mean moves from 0.99 to 0.97 Hz under the first reading. The rescaling does not explain the low rates. (A constant scale within a file multiplies the slopes by a constant, so it changes neither their sign nor their p-values, and the speed counts do not depend on it.) The verifier would call this claim not reproduced; it stays blocked because it depends on speed, for the same reason (Author, step 1.5), and the disagreement is recorded.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

The five questions this attempt asked were answered on 2026-10-20; the answers changed no outcome in the end. After them, grid-phase-orientation was called partially reproduced, an outcome its criterion does not name; the verifier's first round pointed this out, and it is again blocked as methods_underspecified, since both of its parts hold in every layer under 88 of 224 readings and not under the others.

The verifier's first round also asked for outputs, which were added: the gridness of time-shifted spike trains (0.297 of shifted maps have gridness above 0, so the paper's criterion is lax on these data; above the 95% point of the shifted gridness layer III has more grid cells than layer II), the tracking of the two files of rat 11265 that hold every layer II head-direction and conjunctive cell (normal LED geometry; without them layer II has none), the LED geometry of every two-LED file (two files have the LEDs more than 15 cm apart in most samples), the sign test applied in the speed outcome and the electrodes table. The second round agreed with every outcome and asked for more, now added: each (rat, depth, hemisphere, name) counted once for every tested claim but the two that depend on speed (no outcome changes under it), an outcome line in the cells of grid-all-layers, gridness-range-similar and hd-tuning-breadth-layers, which lacked one, pairwise tests locating the gridness-range-similar difference (it lies mostly between layer III and the others), reading (b) of the chi-square for the deep-hd-conjunctive variants, the layer II cells left in the hd-layers variant (6 with plausible tracking), hd-stable-trials without the third file with questionable LED geometry (the circular-correlation reading then fails under two of four readings), and the low-speed rates with the circular files rescaled (no change). The verifier would call speed-slope-steeper partially reproduced and speed-intercept not reproduced; both stay blocked because they depend on speed, as the protocol says, and the disagreement is recorded.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • Each cell-session counts as a cell; the paper's count of 627 cells is about the dandiset's 620 cell-sessions, but some cells may appear in several files.
  • Trials: the 20-minute files are split at the jump in position near 600 s; the 10-minute files are taken as single trials. Positions are smoothed over the whole file, so the 15-point filter spans the join of the two trials for 7 samples on each side, and the pooled maps join two trials whose positions are not centred alike; the first-trial reading of O1 avoids both.
  • Positions are as deposited, rescaled (see the data check); LED1 is taken as the red LED.
  • Details the claims file leaves open and that this attempt fixed as standard choices: contiguous means 4-connected; the block correlation passes when r > 0 with a two-sided p below the level; the small-sample critical value of Watson's one-sample U2 is Stephens'; the circular correlation is Jammalamadaka and SenGupta's; sectors for hd-full-range start at 0 degrees; a spike takes the position of the nearest sample.
  • A peak's centre (its maximum or its centroid) and its radius (of a disc of the same area, or the largest distance to a pixel of the peak) are run as the readings the claims file now names; the central peak takes the same centre and radius.
  • Under the paper's criterion, gridness above 0, this dandiset has more grid cells than the paper reports (277 to 329 against 203), and more in the deeper layers; this shifts every claim built on the grid class. Time-shifted spike trains reach gridness above 0 in 0.297 of maps.
  • Some counts rest on p-values near 0.05 and have differed by a reading or two between runs of the same code on different machines (for example the readings under which both parts of grid-phase-orientation hold, and the t-tests of conj-tuning-similar); no outcome depends on them. The numbers here are this run's.

What this attempt found about the dandiset is listed in the data check: the five findings of the earlier attempt are still present (one, the missing methods, partly fixed by the supplied paper), and the new ones are the rescaled positions, the two trials joined in the 20-minute files with no trial table, the missing distance from the postrhinal border (the electrodes table gives only "MEC"), the missing enclosure and cue-card labels, two two-LED files with the LEDs more than 15 cm apart in most samples, cells without layer, depth or hemisphere, descriptions that disagree with the files, and no statement of which LED is red.
